header: Destinations as cards, one line each
lead: The grid menu: an icon tile, a title and a sentence saying what is behind it, in two to four columns. The whole card is the link, and the title is what a screen reader announces as its name.

items.title: The whole card is the target
items.description: One link per card, spread over the card by the clickable-card rule — no second link to the same page.

items.title: A named nav landmark
items.description: Several menus can sit on one page, so this one is announced by its own heading rather than as “navigation”.

items.title: The icon is decoration
items.description: A tinted tile carrying the semantic key, hidden from assistive technology because the title already says it.

items.title: Two to four columns
items.description: The count is the editor's choice and the grid still reflows on the room it has, not on the width of the window.

items.title: The line is what earns the card
items.description: Destinations whose titles say everything belong in a Link Grid, where no card gets in the way.

items.title: Cells of equal height
items.description: Every card stretches to the tallest of its row, which keeps the icon tiles on one optical line.
